text: Gold closed Tuesday down about 2.6% near $4,032 and silver down about 3.6% near $51.41, as the hotter October inflation report raised the chance of a bigger Fed hike.
The 2-year Treasury yield ended about 17 bp higher at 4.74% and the 10-year about 9 bp higher at 4.99%, also pushed up by a weak 10-year note auction.
Gold miners gave back Monday's jump: GDX closed down 5.4% at $86.51, about twice gold's drop.
Silver funds fell with the metal: SLV closed down 3.45% at $46.48 and the 2x AGQ down 6.86% at $47.39.
Stocks slipped after Monday's big rally: the S&P 500 closed down 0.38% at 7,520.93 and the Nasdaq down 0.74% at 25,065.87, with tech leading the decline.
The dollar index rose about 0.6% to 102.26 and USD/JPY ended near 158.81, close to its high of the day; Bitcoin fell about 1.7% to near $73,766.
Brent settled down 1.17% at $91.49 after briefly dipping below $90 for the first time since August on hopes of an end to the Iran conflict.
